profiles.summary: The endpoint still reports tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97, the newest release in the changelog, with evm2 66687c18 and ruint 1.21.1, and no newer ruint has been published. The Tempo opcode table replaces three entries of the Ethereum table: 0x4f, SSTORE and 0xef. The T14 upgrade, which turns on the 0xef instruction for one fixed account code, activates on mainnet on 8 December 2026, so the deployed network will change after the opcode checks of this cycle.

deltas.delta: tempo_opcode_config sets three instructions over the Ethereum table: millis_timestamp at 0x4f, a Tempo SSTORE that also books storage credits from T7 on, and configurable_account at 0xef. millis_timestamp returns OpcodeNotFound from T1C on, and an eth_call that executes 0x4f now returns OpcodeNotFound as on Ethereum. configurable_account returns OpcodeNotFound unless T14 is active and the running code equals CONFIGURABLE_ACCOUNT_CODE.

T14 activates on mainnet at Unix time 1796742000 (8 December 2026, 15:00 UTC). It adds configurable accounts at existing addresses and changes the gas of second and later calls of a Tempo batch transaction from 2,600 to 100 when the target is already warm.

Tempo main still pins evm2 35aa3280 and ruint 1.21.1, and the v1.19.0 lock pins evm2 66687c18, ruint 1.21.1, alloy-primitives 1.7.3 and fixed-cache 0.1.10, the versions earlier cycles read. The crates.io index lists ruint 1.21.1 as the newest release, with 1.21.0 yanked.

The reth revision of tempo v1.19.0 (31d05e14) already carries the execution cache fix of reth pull request 28148, which keeps the post block storage of an account that a block destroys and creates again.

profiles.summary: Nothing new on gas token or token contracts this cycle; the owner ruled token sweeps out of scope.

The 0xef instruction that T14 enables runs only inside the configurable account code and reads the account configuration commitment. It is not reachable from the PoolManager bytecode, which has no 0xef instruction.

deltas.delta: configurable_account reads the account info of the code address and its configuration commitment; it is gated on T14 and on the running code being CONFIGURABLE_ACCOUNT_CODE.

From v0.8.2 on, opcode.rs differs from v0.8.0 in doc comments only, and evm.rs adds a tracer byte limit, a fork of the inspector instruction loop and a change in how a CallFrom subcall result is reported to tracers. v0.8.5 fixed the reth execution cache, which removed a destroyed account without code from the account cache and kept its old cached storage words when the same block created it again, so later reads served stale values. v0.8.4 fixed an incremental state root computation that could omit a newly inserted entry. Both faults were in v0.8.0 to v0.8.4.

Since v0.8.2, simulation requests that set a block gas limit above --rpc.gascap are refused with error -32602. The official endpoint refuses 33,554,432 gas with the message that the cap is 30,000,000.

The value call hooks of ArcEvm (blocklist check, Transfer log) and the CallFrom subcall path are unchanged in substance from v0.8.0 to v0.8.6; the changes concern tracers.

deltas.delta: checked_frame_init pushes the Transfer log of a value call to an ordinary address after the child frame checkpoint exists and only when the frame did not fail at once; for a precompile it takes its own checkpoint around the log and reverts it when the precompile fails. A reverted value transfer therefore leaves no Transfer log.

findings.title: Arc nodes from v0.8.0 to v0.8.4 could read stale storage of an account without code that a block deleted and created again, which cannot reach PoolManager storage
findings.difference: Arc v0.8.0 to v0.8.4 build on reth v2.2.0, whose execution cache handled an account without code that a block destroyed and created again by removing the account entry and keeping its cached storage words. A later block on that node read the old words. v0.8.5 moved to circlefin/arc-reth v2.2.0-arc.2 with the upstream fix (reth pull request 28148). The v0.8.4 release fixed a separate state root computation fault of the same base.
findings.mechanism: 1. The cache code runs after each block. For an account marked destroyed it checks whether the account had code at the start of the block. With code it clears the whole cache, which is safe. Without code it removed only the account entry and continued, so storage words cached for that address before the block stayed in the cache. 2. Any account can reach the second branch. The v0.8.5 release note names the trigger: a block deletes an empty account under EIP-161 and a later transaction of the same block creates it again and writes storage. A contract destroyed in its own creation transaction and created again in the same block is marked destroyed in the same way. On a node with the fault, a later read of such a word returns the value from before the block, and that node computes a different result from nodes with the fix. 3. The PoolManager has had code since deployment, so a block that touched it in this way would take the first branch and clear the cache. Its slots are keyed by its own address (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364 and the transient libraries such as src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39 index slots under the PoolManager address), so no stale word of another address is read as PoolManager state. 4. Tokens and hooks of pools that do not use attacker-made contracts also have code at the start of any such block. The only contracts whose reads could go stale are contracts created in that pattern, which are attacker-made by construction, and such a contract can return any value to the PoolManager anyway (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-160, src/types/Currency.sol:40-95).
findings.impact: No PoolManager funds move. On a lagging node, a block that uses the pattern makes that node disagree with the rest, which is a liveness and consistency matter for that node's operator and its RPC users. The official endpoint reports v0.8.6-rc1 and publicnode v0.8.5, both with the fix.
findings.preconditions: A validator or RPC node running arc-node v0.8.0 to v0.8.4. Which releases the validators run is not public.
findings.mitigations: Before deployment, confirm with Circle that every validator runs v0.8.5 or later. Integrations that read PoolManager state through RPC should use an endpoint whose arc_getVersion reports v0.8.5 or later.

cleared.check: Tempo's own instruction table: which opcodes Tempo replaces and whether the PoolManager bytecode reaches any of them.
cleared.result: tempo_opcode_config replaces 0x4f, SSTORE and 0xef. A linear disassembly of the 24,009 byte runtime of this checkout's build has no 0x4f and no 0xef instruction, and 0x4f now halts with OpcodeNotFound on the endpoint as on Ethereum. 0xef runs only from T14 and only inside CONFIGURABLE_ACCOUNT_CODE. The Tempo SSTORE stores the same value as the Ethereum one and in addition books storage credits at a separate address and charges state gas, which changes gas and nothing the PoolManager reads back; the 40 SSTORE sites of the bytecode give identical records in all scripts that fit the gas.

cleared.check: Arc releases v0.8.1 to v0.8.6 against the v0.8.0 reading: pinned interpreter and integer library, instruction table, frame hooks for value calls.
cleared.result: The v0.8.6 lock pins the same revm 38.0.0, revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and ruint 1.20.0 as v0.8.0. opcode.rs changes only in doc comments, and the evm.rs changes concern tracer input limits, a fork of the inspector loop and the result tracers see for a CallFrom subcall. SELFDESTRUCT is the only replaced instruction (insert_arc_selfdestruct_instruction), and the PoolManager bytecode has no SELFDESTRUCT. The value call hook keeps the Transfer log inside the frame checkpoint, so a reverted payout from Currency.transfer leaves no log and no balance change (src/types/Currency.sol:40-52).

cleared.check: Whether the stale execution cache fault of reth v2.2.0 (Arc v0.8.0 to v0.8.4) can make a node read a wrong word of PoolManager storage or of a token or hook in a pool without attacker-made contracts.
cleared.result: No. The stale branch applies only to an address without code at the start of the block, destroyed and created again within it. The PoolManager and the contracts of such pools have code, and for a destroyed account with code the cache is cleared as a whole. See the finding for the attacker-made case.

cleared.check: Whether Tempo v1.19.0 carries the execution cache fault of reth pull request 28148.
cleared.result: No. The reth revision 31d05e14 pinned by tempo v1.19.0 has the fixed branch, which keeps the post-block info and storage of a re-created account.

leads.question: Which arc-node release does each Arc validator run, and is every one at v0.8.5 or later?
leads.why: Validators on v0.8.0 to v0.8.4 carry the stale storage and state root faults of reth v2.2.0. The commits that arc_getVersion names on the official endpoint (37812c61) and on dRPC (8e8edb7a) could not be fetched from the public repository, so the reading rests on the v0.8.6 tag.

leads.why: debug_traceCall and debug_traceTransaction on Arc run that fork, so any trace-based evidence on Arc rests on code that block execution does not run.

leadResults.answer: The official endpoint answers arc_getVersion with git_version v0.8.6-rc1, commit 37812c61; publicnode answers v0.8.5 (602eed3b) and dRPC v0.8.6 (8e8edb7a). The v0.8.6 tag still pins revm 38.0.0, revm-interpreter 35.0.1 and ruint 1.20.0 and replaces only SELFDESTRUCT, so the reading in OPCODES.md describes the running release for arithmetic, jumps and memory. Corrections: reth/v2.2.0-508cbdf is circlefin/arc-reth v2.2.0-arc.2 (used from v0.8.5), and v0.8.4 and v0.8.5 fixed two reth state faults, recorded as an operator level information finding. The two commits themselves could not be fetched from the public repository.

From the 6 million block window of cycle 11 (blocks 44,393,309 to 50,393,308), 104 removals and collections that are the only ModifyLiquidity of their transaction were rerun one by one with analyze.py: 103 were checked and 1 set aside because another event touched the pool in the block. All 103 paid both currencies exactly as the source owes (82 removals, 21 collections), the fee growth inside equals the stored value and the position liquidity after equals the prediction in every case. 60 carried nonzero fees, from 17 different senders, in blocks 44,434,210 to 50,147,690, and all 60 are exact. Data in research/network-risk/cycles/013/stablecoin-l1.work/raw/l644-4217.json and raw/l644-senders.json.
